# Copilot prompts: build and run the Enterprise PMO hub

<!-- Generated by tools/build_copilot_prompts.py from sharepoint/list-schema.json and
     solution-config.json. Don't edit by hand: change the script and re-run it. -->

These prompts rebuild the Enterprise PMO hub **by hand in a tenant with Copilot**. Use them
where the packaged route (import the solution, run `Provision-PMOHub.ps1`) isn't possible,
to make a variation, or to give someone a head start in a sandbox. Parts C and D are prompts
for **running** the hub once it is live.

**The repository is the specification.** Copilot output varies between runs and tenants.
After each build, check the result against the spec named under the prompt:

- the flow JSON in `powerautomate/flows/`
- `sharepoint/list-schema.json`
- `sharepoint/dashboard.json`

The imported solution has been through the repository's static checks, but nothing has run
in a tenant yet. A flow Copilot builds hasn't been checked at all. Before relying on either,
run the tests in `DEPLOY-AND-TEST.md`.

| Part | Copilot | Builds |
|------|---------|--------|
| A | Copilot in Microsoft Lists / SharePoint | The 10 lists and libraries, the formatting, the hub page |
| B | Copilot in Power Automate | Flows 01–05 |
| C | Copilot Studio (and Forms) | Ways to submit a risk without opening SharePoint |
| D | Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat | Running the hub: commentary, Steering Committee packs, RAID hygiene |

General rules for every prompt:

- **Internal names:** paste the prompt as written, so the internal names match what the flows
  read.
- **Build order:** create the lists in the order given; the lookups point at PMO Workstreams.
- **Flow owner:** build flows signed in as the named PMO flow owner, never a shared or service
  account (policy D-03).
- **Testing:** leave every flow off until it has been checked against the spec and tested.

## Part A: SharePoint

### A0 Site

```text
Create a SharePoint communication site called "Enterprise PMO" at /sites/EnterprisePMO for the
Project Management Office's portfolio governance. Set the time zone to (UTC+00:00) Dublin,
Edinburgh, Lisbon, London.
```

### A1.1 PMO Workstreams

Where: **Microsoft Lists > New list > Describe your list with Copilot** on the PMO site.

```text
Create a list called "PMO Workstreams" on this site, at the address Lists/PMOWorkstreams.
Purpose: One row per portfolio workstream. Every RAID item, action, change request and document points at one. Flow 02 loops over the active rows. The RAG columns feed the Power BI scorecard.
Keep the built-in Title column. Add these columns, using exactly these internal names, because
Power Automate flows read them by internal name:
- Workstream code (internal name WorkstreamCode): single line of text; required
- Sponsor (internal name Sponsor): person (people only)
- Workstream lead (internal name WorkstreamLead): person (people only)
- Active (internal name Active): yes/no; default Yes
- Overall RAG (internal name OverallRAG): choice; choices "Red", "Amber", "Green"
- Schedule RAG (internal name ScheduleRAG): choice; choices "Red", "Amber", "Green"
- Budget RAG (internal name BudgetRAG): choice; choices "Red", "Amber", "Green"
- Scope RAG (internal name ScopeRAG): choice; choices "Red", "Amber", "Green"
- Status summary (internal name StatusSummary): multiple lines of plain text
Turn on version history. Don't add any other columns.
```

Where: **Microsoft Lists > New list > Describe your list with Copilot** on the PMO site.

```text

Purpose: Risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies for every workstream. Items flagged Escalated to Executive Board show on the hub and in the daily digest when overdue.

- Date pushes (internal name DatePushCount): number; default 0; hidden from the new and edit forms (a flow writes it)
- Original baseline date (internal name OriginalTargetDate): date only; hidden from the new and edit forms (a flow writes it)
- Last date push (internal name LastPushNote): multiple lines of plain text; hidden from the new and edit forms (a flow writes it)
- Tracked date (flow) (internal name TrackedDueDate): single line of text; hidden from the new and edit forms (a flow writes it)
- Tracked status (flow) (internal name TrackedStatus): single line of text; hidden from the new and edit forms (a flow writes it)
```

### A2 Column formatting

The JSON is in the repo. Don't have Copilot write it again. Open each list, then
*column header > Column settings > Format this column > Advanced mode*, and paste:

- `sharepoint/rag-format.json` on RAG rating, Overall RAG, Schedule RAG, Budget RAG and
  Scope RAG
- `sharepoint/due-date-format.json` on Target resolution date (Master RAID Log) and Due date
  (Action and Decision Tracker)
- `sharepoint/status-format.json` on Change Requests Status and RAID Escalation status

To change the colours or wording, ask Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat:

```text
Here is a SharePoint JSON column formatter: [paste the file]. Change it so that [what you
want]. Keep the $schema line, keep the text always visible so colour never carries the meaning
alone, and use only elmType, txtContent, style and attributes supported by the
column-formatting schema v2. Return only the JSON.
```

## Part B: Power Automate flows

Where: **make.powerautomate.com > Create > Describe it to design it**, inside a solution, signed
in as the PMO flow owner. Each prompt is one flow. When Copilot has drafted it:

1. Open every action and check the site, list and column names.
2. Check every filter query and condition against the flow JSON named under the prompt.
3. Turn on concurrency control and trigger conditions where the prompt asks for them. Copilot
   often misses both.

Use environment variables for the site URL, mailboxes and Teams IDs, as listed in
`solution-config.json`.

### B1 Flow 01: Daily executive overdue digest

```text
Build a scheduled cloud flow "PMO 01 - Daily executive overdue digest" that runs Monday to Friday
at 07:00 (GMT Standard Time), one run at a time.
1. Stop unless the environment variable DigestEnabled is Yes.
2. Work out today's date in UK time (yyyy-MM-dd) and the start of today in UK time converted to UTC.
3. In parallel, get items from the PMO site:
   a. Master RAID Log where Status ne 'Closed' and EscalatedToExecutiveBoard eq 1 and
      TargetResolutionDate lt [start of today UTC], ordered by TargetResolutionDate.
   b. Action and Decision Tracker where Status ne 'Completed' and DecisionForum eq 'Executive Board'
      and DueDate lt [start of today UTC], ordered by DueDate.
   Turn on pagination for both.
4. If both are empty, stop. If the PMO Digest History list already has an item titled
   "digest|[today]", stop (one digest a day).
5. Create a PMO Digest History item: Title "digest|[today]", DigestDate now, Status "Posting",
   EscalationsCount and ActionsCount.
6. With Select, turn the first 20 of each result into title/value
   pairs: title = the Workstream lookup's Value; value = "RAID-[ID] [Title] | Owner: [Owner
   display name] | Target: [date dd MMM yyyy, UK] | RAG: [RAGRating Value]" (and
   "ACT-[ID] [Title] | [Category] | Assigned: [AssignedOwner] | Due: [date]" for actions).
7. Post an adaptive card (v1.4) as the Flow bot in the Steering Committee channel (SteerCoTeamId,
   SteerCoChannelId): an attention-style header "GOVERNANCE ALERT / Daily executive overdue
   digest", a summary line with both counts, a FactSet for each section (or "None - Nothing
   overdue"), "...and N more" when a list was cut, and an Open PMO Governance Hub button.
8. If the post succeeds set the history item to "Posted". If it fails set it to "Failed" and email
   PMOOwnerEmail that the digest wasn't posted and why.
Put the steps in a Scope; after it, a second Scope that runs only if the first failed or timed out
and emails PMOOwnerEmail "Flow failed" with the run link.
```

Spec: `powerautomate/flows/01-Daily-Executive-Digest.json`.

### B2 Flow 02: Predictive early warning

```text
Build a scheduled cloud flow "PMO 02 - Predictive early warning", Mondays 06:00 GMT Standard Time.
1. Compose: now, now minus 7 days, now minus 6 days, now minus ChurnWindowDays (default
   14), now plus 10 days, start of today (UK), and today's date yyyy-MM-dd.
2. In parallel get items (with pagination): PMO Workstreams where Active eq 1; Master RAID Log
   where (RAIDType eq 'Risk' or RAIDType eq 'Issue') and (Status ne 'Closed' or ClosedDate ge
   [minus 7d]); Action and Decision Tracker where Status ne 'Completed' or CompletedDate ge
   [minus 7d]; PMO Date Push Log where Created ge [minus churn window]; PMO Trend Snapshots where
   SnapshotDate ge [minus 6d].
3. Apply to each workstream (one at a time). Filter each array by Workstream Id = the
   workstream's ID and count:
   new risks/issues (Created in 7 days); closed (Status Closed and ClosedDate in 7 days); open Red
   and open Amber; actions opened in 7 days; actions closed (Completed, CompletedDate in 7 days);
   open actions due between today and 10 days ahead; date pushes; and pushes whose
   PushesInWindow >= ChurnThreshold (default 2).
4. Net risk velocity = new - closed. Burn-down ratio = closed actions / (opened + due), or 1 when
   the divisor is 0.
5. Flags: RVEL-HIGH when velocity >= RiskVelocityThreshold (2);
   ABD-SLO when ratio < BurnDownThresholdPercent/100 (75%) and at
   least BurnDownMinActionsDue (3) actions are due; CHURN-CRIT when
   any push reached the churn threshold. Score = number of flags (0-3). Write a plain-English
   reason for each flag.
6. If the workstream has no snapshot in the last 6 days, create a PMO Trend Snapshots item with
   all the counts, the ratio, the score, the codes and the reason.
7. If the score >= EarlyWarningThreshold (2) and EarlyWarningEnabled
   is Yes, post a warning-style adaptive card to the PMO Risk Advisory channel with the
   workstream, score, codes, date and reason, then set AdvisoryPosted to Yes on the snapshot.
Wrap in a main Scope with a failure-alert Scope as in flow 01.
```

Spec: `powerautomate/flows/02-Predictive-Early-Warning.json`.

### B3 Flows 03a and 03b: Date churn trackers

```text
Build an automated cloud flow "PMO 03a - Master RAID Log date churn tracker" triggered by the
SharePoint "When an item is created or modified" trigger on the Master RAID Log, one run at a time.
Add this trigger condition so the flow never re-triggers on its own update:
@or(not(equals(coalesce(triggerBody()?['TargetResolutionDate'], 'none'), coalesce(triggerBody()?['TrackedDueDate'], ''))), not(equals(coalesce(triggerBody()?['Status']?['Value'], ''), coalesce(triggerBody()?['TrackedStatus'], ''))))
1. Previous date = TrackedDueDate unless it is empty or 'none'. It is a push when previous and the
   new TargetResolutionDate both exist and the new one is later.
2. If it is a push: count PMO Date Push Log items for this item (SourceList 'Master RAID Log',
   SourceItemId = ID) created in the last ChurnWindowDays, then create a PMO Date Push Log item with
   SourceList, SourceItemId, Workstream, PreviousDate, NewDate, DaysPushed, PushedBy (the editor's
   name) and PushesInWindow = that count + 1.
3. Always update the item (passing Title, Type, Workstream and Status back unchanged):
   TrackedDueDate = TargetResolutionDate as text (or 'none'); TrackedStatus = Status;
   OriginalTargetDate = keep if set, otherwise previous date, otherwise the current date;
   ClosedDate = now if Status just became Closed, otherwise unchanged; DatePushCount + 1 on a push;
   LastPushNote = "Target date moved from [old] to [new] (+N days) by [editor] on [now] UK time."
   on a push.
```

For **03b**, use the same prompt with these swaps:

| In 03a | In 03b |
|--------|--------|
| Action and Decision Tracker in place of Master RAID Log | |
| TargetResolutionDate | DueDate |
| OriginalTargetDate | OriginalDueDate |
| Closed / ClosedDate | Completed / CompletedDate |
| Required columns Type and Workstream | Category, Workstream, Decision forum |

Spec: `powerautomate/flows/03a-RAID-Date-Churn.json` and `03b-Action-Date-Churn.json`.

### B4 Flow 04: Change request approval

```text
Build an automated cloud flow "PMO 04 - Change request approval" triggered when an item is created
in the Change Requests list.
Initialise variables Outcome ("Decision overdue"), DecidedBy, Comments, Forum ("PMO").
1. Stop unless CRApprovalsEnabled is Yes.
2. Reference = CRReference, or "CR-" + the ID padded to 3 digits. It needs the Steering Committee
   when Change type is Scope or Multiple, or the absolute Budget impact is over CRBudgetTolerance
   (default 25000), or Schedule impact (days) is over
   CRScheduleToleranceDays (default 10).
3. Update the item: Status "Under review - PMO", CRReference, DecisionRoute ("PMO" or "Steering
   Committee"), passing the required columns back unchanged.
4. In a Scope: start and wait for an approval (Approve/Reject, first to respond) assigned to
   CRPMOApproverEmails, with the reference, workstream, type, budget and schedule impact,
   change, justification, impact and requester in the details and a link to the item; set its
   timeout to 14 days. Record the responder and comments. If approved and it needs the Steering
   Committee: set Forum to "Steering Committee", re-read the item, set Status "Under review -
   Steering Committee", then a second approval to CRSteerCoApproverEmails (timeout 21 days).
   Outcome: Approved / Rejected; "Returned to requester" if the PMO rejects; "Decision overdue"
   if an approval times out (add a step that runs only on timeout so the scope still succeeds).
5. Re-read the item. If its Status is now Withdrawn keep Withdrawn, otherwise write the outcome,
   DecidedBy, DecisionDate (now) and DecisionNote.
6. If Approved or Rejected: create an Action and Decision Tracker item (Category "Decision Made",
   same Workstream, Decision forum = Forum, Status Completed, Due date today, outcome text) and
   email the requester (Requested by, else the creator). Otherwise email the requester and
   PMOOwnerEmail that it was returned or is overdue.
Main Scope plus failure-alert Scope as in flow 01.
```

Spec: `powerautomate/flows/04-Change-Request-Approval.json`.

### B5 Flow 05: Risk and issue escalation request

```text
Build an automated cloud flow "PMO 05 - Risk and issue escalation request" triggered when an item
is created or modified in the Master RAID Log, with the trigger condition
@and(equals(triggerBody()?['EscalationRequested'], true), not(equals(triggerBody()?['EscalatedToExecutiveBoard'], true)), contains(createArray('Not requested', 'Declined', 'Not decided', ''), coalesce(triggerBody()?['EscalationStatus']?['Value'], '')))
Initialise variables Outcome ("Not decided"), DecidedBy, Comments.
1. Get the item again. Continue only if Request Executive Board escalation is still Yes, Escalation
   status isn't Requested and it isn't already escalated.
2. Claim it: "Send an HTTP request to SharePoint", POST to
   _api/web/lists/GetByTitle('Master RAID Log')/items([ID]) with headers X-HTTP-Method MERGE,
   IF-MATCH = the item's @odata.etag, body {"EscalationStatus":"Requested"}, no retries. If it
   fails with 412 stop quietly (another run claimed it); any other failure emails PMOOwnerEmail.
3. In a Scope: approval (Approve/Reject, first to respond) to EscalationApproverEmails with the
   item's ID, title, type, RAG, workstream, owner, target date, "Why it needs the Board",
   description and who asked; timeout 3 days, with a timeout-only step. Outcome Approved or
   Declined.
4. Re-read the item and update it (required columns unchanged): Escalation status = Outcome,
   Escalated to Executive Board = (Outcome is Approved), Request Executive Board escalation =
   (Outcome is Approved), Escalation decision = "[Outcome] by [who] on [date] UK time: [comments]".
5. If Approved and EscalationAlertsEnabled is Yes, post an attention-style adaptive card "NEW
   EXECUTIVE ESCALATION" to the Steering Committee channel with type, RAG, workstream, owner,
   approver and what the Board needs to do.
6. Email the person who ticked the box and the item owner the outcome (and PMOOwnerEmail if not
   decided), saying how to ask again.
Main Scope plus failure-alert Scope as in flow 01.
```

Spec: `powerautomate/flows/05-Risk-Escalation-Request.json`.

## Part C: Ways to submit a risk

The built-in route needs no extra build. The **Submit Risk / Issue Escalation** quick link
opens the Master RAID Log form. The person fills it in, ticks **Request Executive Board
escalation** and says why. Flow 05 then gets the Head of PMO's decision within 3 days.

Two optional routes for people who don't work in SharePoint both create the same RAID item,
so flows 03a and 05 treat them all the same.

### C1 Copilot Studio agent in Teams: "PMO Risk Desk"

Where: **copilotstudio.microsoft.com > Create > New agent**, in the same environment as the
solution. Describe it with:

```text
Create an agent called "PMO Risk Desk" for programme staff in Microsoft Teams. It helps people
report a risk or issue to the Enterprise PMO and, when it is serious, ask for it to go to the
Executive Board. It is polite, brief and asks one question at a time.
It collects: whether it is a Risk or an Issue; a short title; which workstream (from the PMO
Workstreams list, active only); what is happening and the impact; RAG rating (Red, Amber or Green,
explaining each in one line); who owns it (default: the person reporting); the target resolution
date; and whether it needs the Executive Board, and if so what the Board must decide or unblock
and by when.
It reads the answers back, asks for confirmation, then creates the item in the Master RAID Log
on the PMO site and gives the person the item link and ID. If they asked for the Board, it says the
Head of PMO will decide within 3 working days and they will get an email.
It never edits or closes existing items, never sets "Escalated to Executive Board" itself, and
says it can't help with anything other than reporting risks and issues, pointing to the PMO
hub for everything else.
Knowledge: the Governance Framework and SOPs library on the PMO site, to answer "what counts as
a risk vs an issue" and "when should I escalate".
```

Then add the tool that creates the item. Under *Tools > Add a tool > New agent flow*, describe
it with:

```text
An agent flow "Create RAID item" with inputs RAIDType, Title, WorkstreamId (number), Description,
RAGRating, OwnerEmail, TargetResolutionDate, EscalationRequested (yes/no) and
EscalationJustification. It creates an item in the Master RAID Log on the PMO site with those
values (Status "Open"), and returns the item ID and a link to its display form. It does not set
Escalated to Executive Board or Escalation status.
```

Use a **Get items** on PMO Workstreams (Active eq 1) to offer the workstream as a choice. In
the tool's settings, make it run with the **agent author's** connection (the named PMO flow
owner). Publish the agent to Teams for the programme's security group only.

### C2 Microsoft Forms

Where: **forms.office.com > New form > Draft with Copilot**:

```text
Create a short form "Report a risk or issue to the PMO" with: Risk or Issue (choice); Title (short
text); Workstream (choice: [paste the active workstream names]); What is happening and the impact
(long text); RAG rating (Red, Amber, Green, with a one-line description of each); Target
resolution date (date); Does this need the Executive Board? (Yes/No); If yes, what must the Board
decide or unblock, and by when? (long text, shown only when Yes). Only people in my organisation
can respond, and record their name.
```

Then build a flow in Copilot in Power Automate:

```text
When a new response is submitted to the "Report a risk or issue to the PMO" form, get the response
details, find the PMO Workstreams item whose Title equals the chosen workstream, and create a
Master RAID Log item: Type, Title, Workstream (lookup Id), Description, RAG rating, Owner = the
responder, Target resolution date, Status "Open", Request Executive Board escalation and Why it
needs the Board from the answers. Email the responder the new item's link.
```

Workstream choices in a form don't update themselves. When a workstream is added or closed,
update the form too. The agent (C1) reads the list, so it doesn't have this problem.

## Part D: Running the hub with Microsoft 365 Copilot

Use these in **Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat** (work mode). Point it at the lists with
`/` references or links. Copilot drafts and the PMO decides: check every figure against the
lists before it goes to the Board.

**Weekly commentary** (for the hub's commentary text part):

```text
Using the Master RAID Log, the Action and Decision Tracker and this week's PMO Trend Snapshots on
the Enterprise PMO site, draft the "PMO executive commentary" for the hub in under 150 words:
current governance focus with the RAG split across active workstreams; the two or three primary
escalations (item, impact, intervention needed); and a numbered list of the decisions the Executive
Board must take before the next Steering Committee, with CR references. Plain English, no
adjectives without a fact behind them.
```

**Steering Committee pre-read:**

```text
Prepare a one-page pre-read for the Steering Committee on [date]: change requests "Under review -
Steering Committee" (reference, change, budget and schedule impact, PMO comments); RAID items
escalated to the Executive Board that are Red or overdue; Executive Board decisions due; and any
workstream with an early warning score of 2 or more this week and why. Use a table per section and
cite the list item for every line.
```

**RAID hygiene check:**

```text
Look at open items in the Master RAID Log and list the ones that need attention: no owner, no
target date, Red with no mitigation, target date pushed two or more times (Date pushes), or not
modified in 30 days. Group by workstream and say what is missing for each.
```

**Change request summary for an approver:**

```text
Summarise change request [CR-nnn] for an approver in five bullet points: what changes, why, the
budget and schedule impact against tolerance, the risks if approved and if rejected, and what the
PMO review said.
```
